title: Weekend fragments: those inadvertent touches and thoughts
summary: This blog post records the author’s weekend full of observations, thoughts and emotions. The article begins with an encounter with a woman on the subway who faces scars optimistically, eliciting insights into a positive attitude towards life. Then, the author shared his experience in an amusement park, observing that male parents were less involved in parent-child interactions, and challenged the high-altitude ropeway, from which he realized the importance of focusing on the present.
markdown:
![image]()
Last weekend, my family and I spent a quite ordinary time, but in these daily fragments, I unexpectedly captured some special moments. They were like pebbles, quietly causing ripples in my heart, and I couldn't help but want to record these insights.

On Saturday morning, our family of three took the subway to the amusement park. People were coming and going in the carriage, but my eyes unconsciously stopped on a lady. There is a very obvious scar on the right side of her chin. To be honest, when I first saw it, I felt a little sorry for her. But when I looked again, I saw that she was talking and laughing with the people around her, with that kind of smile that stretched from the inside out on her face, her eyes were full of light, and she didn't appear to be embarrassed or uncomfortable at all because of the scar. At that moment, my heart was really touched - isn't this how we should live most? There will always be "marks" of one kind or another in life (some are visible, some are hidden in the heart), but the most important thing is whether you can accept them calmly and still love life. Optimism can really make people shine in any situation.
When I arrived at the amusement park, I discovered a very interesting phenomenon: looking around, there were a lot of mothers with their babies, but where were the fathers? Relatively rare. Most dads have found a corner, sitting or lying down, with their phones in hand, immersed in their own world. I feel a little pity for them - in this way, do I miss a lot of deeply interactive and happy moments with my children? My little guy didn't care so much. He went straight to his favorite car as soon as he arrived. His pure energy was really enviable. Later, I decided to challenge the high-altitude ropeway. It is the kind of project that requires you to wear safety ropes and safety straps, walk on a single-plank bridge at a high place, and cross obstacles. To be honest, I am a little afraid of heights. But the strange thing is that when I actually traveled high in the sky, I didn't feel particularly scared. Maybe my shortsightedness "helped" - because I can't see how high my feet are, but I can focus more clearly on every pedal in front of me and how to take each step. This kind of "unable to see" concentration actually alleviated my fear. This suddenly made me think, isn’t life the same? Sometimes, when we think too much about the uncertainty of the future, we become handcuffed. Perhaps, by focusing on the present moment and focusing on every step in front of you, you can walk more steadily and further, and even find unexpected peace and strength.

Then, I played with my son in the playground. While playing, I noticed that there were some children around me, and their eyes showed the longing for their parents' company. There was a little girl who ran to her father several times to ask him to play with her, but her father always waved his hand and refused at first. It wasn't until the little girl was about to cry that her father reluctantly moved with her a few times. Seeing this scene, I felt very sad for the children - the children can feel that perfunctory companionship, and it simply cannot satisfy their deep desire for closeness and interaction. Later, my son's little friend also came, and the two little guys quickly played together and laughed constantly. I also joined them. Unexpectedly, the three of us (the two little ones and me, the older one) were so involved in playing that we actually attracted the attention of other children! One after another they came running over, all clamoring to join us. There was a little girl among them who was so cute that she almost became my "little tail". She followed me all the time and insisted on playing with me. Thus, a vigorous game of "Police Catch Thief" began, and I, the "old father", instantly transformed into the "King of Children"! Being chased by a group of lively children, although I was so tired that I was sweating profusely and finally collapsed on the ground unable to move, but looking at the pure smiles on their faces and their whole-hearted enthusiasm, I felt really full of satisfaction and accomplishment. That little girl was taken away by her mother until she was about to go home. Her reluctant eyes still feel very heart-warming when I think about it. At that moment, I truly felt how important parents’ companionship is to children. It is not only an investment of time, but also the establishment of emotional connection and trust.

This trip to the amusement park gave me a deeper understanding of the word "company". Children really don’t need expensive toys or a big amusement park. What they long for most is actually playing with their parents, laughing together, and creating those unique memories together. This high-quality companionship not only gives them a sense of security, but also subtly shapes their character, allowing them to learn how to get along with others, and also leaves them with the most precious mark of their childhood. Although I can't change others (after all, every family has its own pattern), what I can do is try my best to spend more time with my child and truly participate in his growth. Because I know that this companionship is more precious than any material wealth.

On Sunday, my wife and I changed our moods and went to the cinema to watch "F1: The Furious." Wow, that scene was so shocking! The roar of the engine, the sense of speed of the racing car whizzing by, and the tense atmosphere of the entire race all make people feel immersed in the scene. If you also like that kind of speed and passion, I highly recommend you to experience it, it is definitely worth the price of admission!

In this way, a weekend full of observation, thinking, sweat and emotion came to an end in the afterglow of Fast and Furious. It may not be the textbook "perfect" kind, but it is these inadvertent discoveries and touches that make it particularly meaningful in my heart. Isn't life made up of these small, shining moments?
sourceTitle: 周末碎片：那些不经意的触动与思考
